Subject: Post-demo recap — compute island qualification & next steps

Hi Sofia / Danielle,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. I've attached a short scope + SLA outline and a ballpark estimate.

Key pain points we heard
- Unpredictable latency spikes on your current multi-tenant endpoints (p95 spikes to 1.2s during heavy batches).
- Need strict isolation for PHI-sensitive workloads and auditability (retention and KMS controls).
- Short bursts for synchronous inference (site search & clinical extraction) mixed with longer batch jobs for model training/evals.

Goals we agreed on
- Dedicated compute pool with tenant isolation for production models (initial target: 4–6 H100-equivalent slots).
- P95 latency target: <250ms for short payloads (<=512 tokens) and clear throughput baseline for batch jobs.
- SLA expectations: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool, with an operational runbook and on-call escalation.
- Timeline: procurement & PO target in Q3; production readiness in Q4 with a gradual canary.

Technical constraints you mentioned
- On-prem data residency for a subset of jobs — will need VPC/private deployment for PHI; hosted Dedicated OK for non-PHI.
- Preference for quantized model profiles to reduce unit cost but want to validate quality on representative prompts.

Proposed next steps (owner / by when)
1) Redwood technical deep dive (Rishi) — schedule week of Aug 9 to map exact slot sizing and failover topology.
2) Detailed SOW & SLA draft (Grace) — I shared the draft in the attached PDF; will align with procurement on the billing cadence. Target Aug 6.
3) Price & PO template to Procurement (Ben) — Ben to provide reserve vs burst pricing and a PO template for internal review. Target Aug 10.
4) Quality gate: run 500 prompt evals against quantized profile (joint) — deliverable: regression report. Target Aug 24.

Attachments: scope-and-sla-outline.pdf (3 pages), compute-island-estimate.xlsx

If I missed anything obvious, flag it — otherwise I'll schedule the technical deep dive with Rishi for next week.

Best,

Subject: Internal: calc for CedarLake burst / failover options

Grace / Rishi — internal calc and suggestion before the deep dive. Keeping internal so we don't overwhelm procurement with too many variants yet.

Summary of proposed options
A) Reserved baseline (single-tenant pool, 4 H100 slots) + metered burst to a shared pool. Pros: predictable baseline cost, easy isolation. Cons: burst latency varies during peak.

B) Reserved island (6-slot single-tenant pool) with cross-region failover and pre-warmed hot spares (2 slots). Pros: stable p95, minimal noisy neighbor. Cons: higher committed cost.

C) Hybrid (4-slot reserved + 2 pre-warmed burst slots in same tenant + prefix caching for top queries). Middle ground for cost vs p95.

SLA framing suggestion (we'll include in SOW)
- Availability: 99.9% for the reserved pool; we include a per-minute credit mechanism tied to down minutes.
- Latency SLO: p95 <250ms for short payloads when under reserved capacity; during bursts the p95 may degrade but we'll provide fallback routing to a quantized model to keep tail <500ms.

Action items for deep dive (Rishi owner)
- Confirm token distribution and sample traffic (need traces + top 50 prompts).
- Validate prefix/KV caching strategies and how they map to observed p95 spikes.
- Walk through failover runbook and test cadence.

I'll draft a short table of estimated monthly committed spend for A/B/C and drop it into the shared Drive before your SOW draft.

—Ben
